verdict: 2026-07-24 16:46:04 PDT (America/Los_Angeles) — The overall shape is lean and repo-consistent: delete the diagnostic path, make narrow documentation edits, update the transitive dependency through the lockfile, and reuse `express-rate-limit`. I would build it this way after tightening the OAuth state verifier and cookie contract; neither requires a new dependency.

findings.title: State comparison is not defined as a total, non-throwing predicate
findings.claim: The sketch says to call `timingSafeEqual` against the cookie and `req.query.state`, but does not constrain their types or compare buffer lengths first. Express query values can be arrays or other non-string shapes, malformed cookies are attacker-controlled, and Node's `timingSafeEqual` throws when byte lengths differ. An ordinary mismatch could therefore become a 500 instead of AC7's required 400 rejection.
findings.alternative: Create a small verifier that accepts only two non-empty strings, converts both to buffers, returns false when their lengths differ, and performs `timingSafeEqual` only inside a non-throwing path. Treat every absent, duplicate, malformed, array-shaped, or mismatched value as the same 400 result before token exchange, and clear the state cookie on every terminal callback path.
findings.win: Eliminates an attacker-triggerable exception path and centralizes AC7's invariant that every invalid state is rejected before token exchange.

findings.title: The proposed OAuth cookie omits the modern secure-cookie boundary
findings.claim: The stated cookie attributes are `httpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax`, and a short `Max-Age`, but not `Secure`, an explicit path, or a host-only prefix. Because this cookie is the browser-session binding for OAuth CSRF protection, allowing it over HTTP and leaving it open to path/domain cookie shadowing weakens the mechanism. Current cookie guidance recommends `Secure` and a `__Host-` name with `Path=/` and no `Domain`; `SameSite=Lax` remains appropriate for Zoom's cross-site top-level GET callback. See [MDN secure-cookie guidance](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Security/Practical_implementation_guides/Cookies) and [OAuth 2.0 Security BCP](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc9700/).
findings.alternative: Use an opaque cookie such as `__Host-zoom-oauth-state` with `Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Path=/; Max-Age=<short TTL>` and no `Domain`. Use Express's existing `res.cookie` and `res.clearCookie` serialization with identical attributes rather than hand-building `Set-Cookie`; only the narrow inbound lookup needs a defensive parser.
findings.win: Prevents the state cookie from traveling over plaintext HTTP, blocks domain/path cookie shadowing in supporting browsers, and replaces manual response-header serialization with an existing Express construct without adding a dependency.
